science.qualification: Photosphere color from a blackbody at the star's published temperature, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,291 K and log g 4.5 (u1 0.575, u2 0.182): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Sep 2012
science.description: Radial component of the star's large-scale magnetic field, fitted with ZDIpy to 16 ESPaDOnS spectra of 25 September 2012 to 1 October 2012 (reduced chi-square 1.30, against 5.8 with no field); mean field 69 G. A reduction made in this project, not a published map. Black line: 42 degrees south, below which the star never faces us.
science.title: ESPaDOnS · magnetic map made here · Sep 2012

science.label: Sector 30
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 3.23 days, fitted with starry to the light curve this project measured from the TESS full-frame images of sector 30 (the light swings by 4.9%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.35%, the light's own noise being 0.10%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. The map is made at the tilt the page draws the star with, 42°. Gaia DR3 lists 3 other stars within 63 arcseconds, giving 0.57% of the light in the star's pixels. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 30

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffeada, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 30 (September and October 2020): the map's scale, 88% to 112% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 20.2% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · September and October 2020
